newsitem.title: UK: ASDA eyes speeding change, yr profits rise.
newsitem.headline: ASDA eyes speeding change, yr profits rise.

text.p: British supermarkets retailer ASDA Group Plc turned in a strong year's sales performance on Thursday and chief executive Allan Leighton said it could do much more and "accelerate the rate of change and innovation still further."

ASDA, which aims to be the cheapest of the UK's four big supermarkets, said same store sales increased 9.2 percent as it reported year pretax profits before exceptional items up 16 percent to 353.7 million pounds ($588.1 million) and paid out a dividend of 3.05 pence per share, up 15 percent.

ASDA said its market share had grown to 11 percent from 10.1 percent a year ago as it focused on low prices and innovation, adding that it had widened the price gap with competitors to eight percent "while holding a stable gross margin."

The company, known for its cheeky innovations and style as a consumers' champion, said sales of its own-brand goods accounted for 38 percent of total sales, putting it on track to meet its target of 40 percent of total in 1998.

ASDA said it would drive forward renewal of stores, its prime source of sales growth. It said it intended to open 10 new stores in 1998, adding to its existing 213 stores, but expected capital expenditure to be marginally lower than the 481 million pounds last year.

"Our management principles of pace, simplicity and motivation guide our actions in a mature market with slow growth and increasing complexity," said Archie Norman, ASDA's entrepreneurial chairman who has just been elected as a member of parliament for the opposition Conservative party.
